topic.name: The Components of a Vector with Respect to an Orthogonal or Orthonormal Basis

question.text: Given the orthonormal basis $\mathcal{B}=\left\{\begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{26}} \\ -\dfrac{5}{\sqrt{26}} \end{bmatrix},\begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{26}} \\ \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{26}} \end{bmatrix}\right\}$ of $\mathbb R^2,$ find $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}$ if $\mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} -5 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}.$
question.explanation:
Let's denote the vectors of $\mathcal{B}$ as $\mathbf{q}_1,\, \mathbf{q}_2.$

Since $\mathcal{B}$ is an orthonormal basis, we have that $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix}$, where $x_i = \mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{q}_i.$ Computing the components of $\mathbf{x},$ we get the following:

\begin{align*} x_1 &= \begin{bmatrix} -5 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{26}} \\ -\dfrac{5}{\sqrt{26}} \end{bmatrix}= -\dfrac{5}{\sqrt{26}}-\dfrac{5}{\sqrt{26}} = -\dfrac{10}{\sqrt{26}}\\[5pt] x_2 &= \begin{bmatrix} -5 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{26}} \\ \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{26}} \end{bmatrix}= -\dfrac{25}{\sqrt{26}}+\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{26}}=-\dfrac{24}{\sqrt{26}} \end{align*}

Therefore, we have \[[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} -\dfrac{10}{\sqrt{26}} \\ -\dfrac{24}{\sqrt{26}} \end{bmatrix}.\]

example.title: Calculating the Components of a Vector With Respect to a Given Orthonormal Basis

question.text: Given the orthonormal basis $\mathcal{B}$ of $\mathbb{R}^3$ and the vector $\mathbf{x}$ below, find the value of $\dfrac{x_2}{4}$, where $x_2$ is the second component of $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}.$ \[ \mathcal{B}=\left\{\begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ 0 \\ \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \end{bmatrix}, \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\end{bmatrix}, \begin{bmatrix} -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}} \end{bmatrix}\right\}, \qquad \mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} 2\sqrt{6} \\ 3\sqrt{6} \\ \sqrt{6} \end{bmatrix} \]
question.explanation:
Let's denote the vectors of $\mathcal{B}$ as $\mathbf{q}_1,\, \mathbf{q}_2,\, \mathbf{q}_3.$

Since $\mathcal{B}$ is an orthonormal basis, we have that $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}$, where $x_i = \mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{q}_i.$ Computing $x_2,$ we obtain

\begin{align*} x_2 &= \mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{q}_2 \\[5pt] &= \begin{bmatrix} 2\sqrt{6} \\ 3\sqrt{6} \\ \sqrt{6} \end{bmatrix} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] &= 2\sqrt{2} + 3\sqrt{2} - \sqrt{2} \\[5pt] &= 4\sqrt{2}. \end{align*}

Therefore, \[\dfrac{x_2}{4}=\dfrac{4\sqrt{2}}{4}=\sqrt{2}.\]

example.title: Calculating the Components of a Vector With Respect to a Given Orthonormal Basis

question.text: Given the orthogonal basis $\mathcal{B}$ of $\mathbb{R}^3$ and the vector $\mathbf{x}$ below, find the value of $3 x_3$, where $x_3$ is the third component of $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}.$ \[ \mathcal{B}=\left\{\begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix},\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -4 \\ 7 \end{bmatrix},\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}\right\}, \qquad \mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 3 \\ 6 \end{bmatrix} \]
question.explanation:
Let's denote the vectors of $\mathcal{B}$ as $\mathbf{q}_1,\, \mathbf{q}_2,\,\mathbf{q}_3.$

Since $\mathcal{B}$ is an orthogonal basis, we have that $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}$, where $x_i = \dfrac{\mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{q}_i}{\mathbf{q}_i \cdot \mathbf{q}_i}.$ Computing $x_3,$ we obtain

\begin{align*} x_3 &= \dfrac{\mathbf{x}\cdot \mathbf{q}_3}{\mathbf{q}_3 \cdot \mathbf{q}_3} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{4 \cdot 1 + 3 \cdot 2 + 6 \cdot 1}{1^2+2^2+1^2} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{4+6+6}{6} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{8}{3}. \end{align*}

Therefore, \[3 x_3=3 \cdot \dfrac{8}{3} =8.\]

example.title: Finding a Component of a Vector With Respect to a Given Orthogonal Basis

question.text: Given the orthogonal basis $\mathcal{B}$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ and the vector $\mathbf{x}$ below, find the value of $15x_2,$ where $x_2$ is the second component of $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}.$ \[ \mathcal{B}=\left\{\begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}, \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}\right\}, \qquad \mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} 10 \\ -15 \end{bmatrix} \]
question.explanation:
Let's denote the vectors of $\mathcal{B}$ as $\mathbf{q}_1,\, \mathbf{q}_2.$

Since $\mathcal{B}$ is an orthogonal basis, we have that $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix}$, where $x_i = \dfrac{\mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{q}_i}{\mathbf{q}_i \cdot \mathbf{q}_i}.$ Computing $x_2,$ we obtain

\begin{align*} x_2 &= \dfrac{\mathbf{x}\cdot \mathbf{q}_2}{\mathbf{q}_2 \cdot \mathbf{q}_2} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{10 \cdot 4 + (-15) \cdot 3}{4^2+3^2} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{40-45}{25} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{-5}{25}\\[5pt] &= -\dfrac15. \end{align*}

Therefore, \[15x_2=15 \cdot \left(-\dfrac{1}{5}\right)=-3.\]

example.title: Finding a Component of a Vector With Respect to a Given Orthogonal Basis

question.text: Given the orthogonal basis $\mathcal{B}$ of $\mathbb{R}^3$ and the vector $\mathbf{x}$ below, find the value of $5 x_3$, where $x_3$ is the third component of $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}.$ \[ \mathcal{B}=\left\{\begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 2 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix},\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix},\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}\right\}, \qquad \mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ -7 \\ 6 \end{bmatrix} \]
question.explanation:
Let's denote the vectors of $\mathcal{B}$ as $\mathbf{q}_1,\, \mathbf{q}_2,\,\mathbf{q}_3.$

Since $\mathcal{B}$ is an orthogonal basis, we have that $[\mathbf{x}]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \\ x_3 \end{bmatrix}$, where $x_i = \dfrac{\mathbf{x} \cdot \mathbf{q}_i}{\mathbf{q}_i \cdot \mathbf{q}_i}.$ Computing $x_3,$ we obtain

\begin{align*} x_3 &= \dfrac{\mathbf{x}\cdot \mathbf{q}_3}{\mathbf{q}_3 \cdot \mathbf{q}_3} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{5 \cdot 2 + (-7) \cdot 1 + 6 \cdot 0}{2^2+1^2+0^2} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{10-7+0}{5} \\[5pt] &=\dfrac{3}{5}. \end{align*}

Therefore, \[5 x_3=5 \cdot \dfrac{3}{5} =3.\]
